Vectorize Rule

Source: R/vectorize.R
rule_vectorize.Rd

Construct the rule vectorize() uses for a primitive applied to values that are mapped over. Inside the rule, such values carry the batch axis as their last axis.

Many primitives (such as elementwise ops) just work as is. For others, some parameters need to be adjusted to account for the added batch axis. This includes shape parameters of axis mappings. The rule is then responsible for rewriting these parameters so that they work correctly with the added batch axis. For the most common cases, see vec_shape() where it is enough to just mark the parameter with the appropriate kind via the params argument. For more complex rules it is necessary to provide the fn argument.

Usage

rule_vectorize(fn = NULL, params = list(), unbatched = integer())

Arguments

fn

(NULL | function)
A rule of its own, for a primitive for which declaring params and unbatched is not enough. If given, the other arguments must be left at their defaults. It is called as fn(inputs, batched, params, size) for every call of the primitive with at least one operand that is mapped over, where

  • inputs is the list of operands, in the order of the primitive's arguments: one that is mapped over with the batch axis as its last axis, the others as they are,

  • batched is a logical() saying which of inputs are mapped over,

  • params is the named list of the parameters of the call, and

  • size is the size of the batch axis.

It returns the outputs of the primitive applied to every slice, as a list in the order of the primitive's outputs, or a single output as it is. Every output has the batch axis as its last axis, also one that is the same for every slice.

params

(named list())
How each parameter with an entry per axis of the operands, or a shape, changes, one of the kinds in vec_shape().

unbatched

(integer())
Positions of the operands that cannot be mapped over, e.g. the padding value of prim_pad(). They are passed on unchanged.

Value

(anvl_rule_vectorize)
A rule to assign to prim_<name>[["vectorize"]].

See also

vectorize(), vec_shape()

Examples

# the rule of prim_transpose()
rule_vectorize(params = list(perm = vec_axis_map()))
#> $fn
#> NULL
#> 
#> $params
#> $params$perm
#> function (x, size) 
#> c(x, length(x) + 1L)
#> <bytecode: 0x5c0b52ebc4e0>
#> <environment: 0x5c0b52ebc7f0>
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "anvl_param_kind"
#> 
#> 
#> $unbatched
#> integer(0)
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "anvl_rule_vectorize"
